title: Hallucination Detection in Large Language Models Using Diversion Decoding
abstract: arXiv:2607.10476v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have emerged as a powerful tool for retrieving knowledge through seamless, human-like interactions. Despite their advanced text generation capabilities, LLMs exhibit hallucination tendencies, where they generate factually incorrect statements and fabricate knowledge, undermining their reliability and trustworthiness. Multiple studies have explored methods to evaluate LLM uncertainty and detect hallucinations. However, existing approaches are often probabilistic and computationally expensive, limiting their practical applicability. In this paper, we introduce diversion decoding, a novel method for developing an LLM uncertainty heuristic by actively challenging model-generated responses during the decoding phase. Through diversion decoding, we extract features that capture the LLM's resistance to produce alternative answers and utilize these features to train a machine-learning model to develop a heuristic

translated_title: 利用分流解码检测大型语言模型中的幻觉
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）已成为通过无缝、类似人类的交互检索知识的强大工具。尽管它们具有先进的文本生成能力，但LLMs表现出幻觉倾向，即生成事实不正确的陈述并虚构知识，这削弱了它们的可靠性和可信度。多项研究探索了评估LLM不确定性和检测幻觉的方法。然而，现有方法通常基于概率且计算成本高昂，限制了其实际应用。在本文中，我们引入了分流解码，一种通过在解码阶段主动挑战模型生成响应来开发LLM不确定性启发式方法的新颖技术。通过分流解码，我们提取捕捉LLM对产生替代答案的抵抗力的特征，并利用这些特征训练机器学习模型以开发一种启发式方法。
tldr: 本文提出了一种名为“分流解码”的新方法，通过解码阶段主动挑战模型响应来提取特征，从而高效检测大型语言模型中的幻觉。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces "diversion decoding," a novel method that extracts features by actively challenging model responses during decoding to efficiently detect hallucinations in large language models.
